title: Letter 28
breadcrumbs: Home > Fathers of the Church > Letters of St. Jerome > Letter 28

paragraphs.text: {{NOTE:note1}} and by Aquila <greek>ἀ</greek> <greek>εί</greek>, was as much a crux in Jerome's day as it is in ours. <quote>Some,</quote> he writes, <quote>make it a 'change of metre,' others 'a pause for breath,' others 'the beginning of a new subject.' According to yet others it has something to do with rhythm or marks a burst of instrumental music.</quote> Jerome himself inclines to follow Aquila and Origen, who make the word mean <quote>forever,</quote> and suggests that it betokens completion, like the <quote>explicit</quote> or <quote>feliciter</quote> in contemporary Latin manuscripts. Written at Rome A.D. 384.

notes.text: An explanation of the Hebrew word Selah. This word, rendered by the LXX. διάψαλμα
